title: Dietary Proteins and Amino Acids

sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of a protein like a beaded necklace. Each little bead is an amino acid, and stringing many beads together makes the whole necklace, which is the protein. Fats and carbs use different kinds of beads, so amino acids are the special beads just for proteins.

### Question 2

Your body is like a kitchen that can cook some ingredients by itself but not others. The ones it can't make have to be bought at the store, which here means eaten in food. Those store-bought-only ingredients are the essential amino acids.

### Question 3

Imagine you need all nine puzzle pieces to finish a picture. A complete protein hands you the whole set in one box. If a food is missing a piece or two, it isn't complete, and you'd have to grab the missing pieces from another food.

### Question 4

The necklace of amino acids is too big to fit through the tiny doors in your gut wall. Digestion snips the string between the beads so each single bead can slip through the door and get used to build brand-new necklaces your body needs.

### Question 5

Animal foods usually bring the whole set of puzzle pieces. A single plant food often shows up short one piece, but a different plant has extra of that piece, so mixing plants fills in what's missing. Same pieces overall, just spread out differently.

### Question 6

Beans are missing one puzzle piece and rice is missing a different one. Eat both and each one hands over the piece the other lacks, so together they make a full picture. They don't even have to be at the same meal, since beans at lunch and rice at dinner works too because your body pools the pieces across the day. That teamwork is what complementary proteins means.

### Question 7

To build a toy car you need four wheels. If you have hundreds of every other part but only three wheels, you can only finish as many cars as your wheels allow. The part you run out of first, the limiting amino acid, decides how much you can build.

### Question 8

Most plant foods bring only part of the puzzle set, but soy is a special plant that brings the whole set by itself. So tofu lets a vegan get every essential piece from one food instead of mixing two.

### Question 9

Your body likes to burn carbs and fat for energy, like using firewood. When the firewood runs out, it starts burning the furniture, meaning your muscles, just to stay warm. Eating enough calories keeps the furniture safe so muscle isn't wasted.

### Question 10

The number of grams just tells you how much protein there is, not how good it is. What makes it top-quality is having every essential puzzle piece. Since this food has them all, it's a complete protein, no partner food needed.

### Question 11

Your body can't keep leftover amino acids in a pantry for later. When you eat more protein than you need, it strips off the nitrogen part, which leaves the body as urea in urine, and then burns or stores the rest, often as fat. So extra protein doesn't simply pile up as muscle.

### Question 12

Every amino acid matters when building a protein, essential or not. The word essential just means 'you must eat it because your body can't make it.' Nonessential ones are still used all the time; your body just knows how to make them itself.
